title: Deprecate ambiguous 429 bodies and introduce structured backoff_hint + idempotency reconciliation for streaming/tool-calls
author: Amelia Chen
release_notes: Add structured 'backoff_hint' to 429/503 responses in OpenAI compatibility layer; clarify idempotency resolution rules for partial/streamed responses; updates SDK compatibility shims and docs. Non-breaking for well-behaved clients but recommends updating retry logic to use new hints.
description:
Motivation: Customers and SDKs have been relying on heterogeneous 429/503 body fields (sometimes human-readable 'retry' messages, sometimes opaque strings). That ambiguity caused inconsistent backoff implementations across SDKs and replay logic failures for streaming tool/function calls where partial frames may have been accepted by downstream services. This PR centralizes a single structured hint field (backoff_hint) in the OpenAI-compat response shape and specifies deterministic idempotency reconciliation when streams end mid-frame.

Design: 1) Response contract: when a request is rate-limited or transient-failed the shim will include 'backoff_hint' in the JSON body (when JSON body allowed) and as a 'x-redwood-backoff' header for non-JSON responses. The backoff_hint uses a small schema {"recommended_ms": <int>, "retry_after_window_ms": <int>, "scope": "client|project|global"} — see docs for exact fields. 2) Idempotency reconciliation: streaming responses now emit a final 'frame_status' marker (ok|partial|failed) in the event stream. If a stream ends with 'partial' and the upstream returned a transient 429/503, the platform will expose reconciliation metadata to help clients decide whether replay is safe. 3) Compatibility: older clients will see a new header but continue to receive existing status codes; no status code changes. SDK gateways (python/ts/go) are updated to prefer backoff_hint when present.

Implementation highlights: - src/openai_shim/error_mapping.go: map internal rate categories to structured hint; add header emission. - runtime/streaming/partial_replay.go: track frame boundaries and emit 'frame_status' trailer. - sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py: higher-level helper parse_backoff_hint() and improved idempotency helper for streamed tool calls. - docs/openai/error-codes.md: new section with examples and recommended client backoff algorithms.

Migration: - Server side will emit backoff_hint as opt-in initially via feature flag (default on for next minor). - Recommend SDKs upgrade: parse header first, then body. Fallback to Retry-After if present. - For customers with custom proxies: ensure x-redwood-backoff header is not stripped.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for mapping logic - [x] End-to-end streaming integration tests that simulate partial frames + 429 - [x] SDK helpers added (py/ts/go) - [x] Docs and upgrade notes - [x] Feature flag for gradual rollout

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing canonical HTTP status codes to preserve backwards compatibility. We add structured hints and stream trailers to allow deterministic client behavior rather than relying on freeform human-readable strings.

review_comments: Samir Patel (request changes): Can we make the header name less vendor-specific? Suggest 'x-backoff-hint' instead of 'x-redwood-backoff' for interoperability. Also add a small fuzz test for malformed backoff hints.

Amelia Chen (author): Kept 'x-redwood-backoff' for now to avoid collisions with existing proxies; added a translation layer that supports 'x-backoff-hint' if present. Added fuzz test for header/body parsing (tests/integration/backoff_fuzz_test.go).
Diego Morales: Please clarify how this interacts with existing Retry-After header—documented but add a short code sample showing fallback ordering.
Amelia Chen: Added code sample to docs and strengthened SDK parsing order: header -> body -> Retry-After.
Lena Hoff (approve): Tests look good and migration path is reasonable. Approving for merge once CI green.
merge_summary: Squashed 5 commits into main; feature flag enabled default-off for 2 weeks, docs published; SDK patch releases queued.
notes_for_cherrypick: Backport to release/1.12 is optional: only if a customer is on private deployment and requests earlier rollout. Backport PR template prepared.
examples_client_snippet:
// pseudocode: prefer header then body then Retry-After
if header 'x-redwood-backoff' present: parse -> use recommended_ms; else if body.backoff_hint present: parse -> use recommended_ms; else if Retry-After present: use Retry-After; otherwise exponential jittered backoff.
test_plan: Run unit + integration suite; coordinate with SDK release team to validate golang/ts/py helpers; roll out feature flag in canary region; monitor for increase in 429s and client replay errors via observability dashboard.
